title: tenant-scoped-gateway-and-gpu-allocator-modules-for-private-deployments
author: Marta Glover
release_notes: Introduce two new Terraform modules (tenant_gateway, gpu_allocator) and a per-tenant remote state prefixing convention plus a migrator utility. Adds best-effort automated route/peering resources, least-privilege IAM bindings for node pools, and an allocation policy that supports soft reserves for burst capacity.
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private asked for clearer tenant boundaries for networking and GPU capacity to reduce blast radius and simplify upgrades. This PR introduces two focused Terraform modules and a small migration helper to move from a single-global layout to tenant-scoped state prefixes.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds modules/tenant_gateway (automates creating a tenant-scoped VPC peering/gateway construct with optional cross-account route table entries and a small set of default egress/NAT rules), and modules/gpu_allocator (provides GPU node pool profiles, node taints/labels, IAM role binding templates for node service accounts, and a soft-reserve allocator that marks capacity slots for priority tenants). Introduces convention: remote state uses prefix = "tenants/<tenant_id>/env/<env>" and a migrator script tools/migrate-per-tenant-state that copies state files, rewrites backend keys, and rebinds DynamoDB locks with a dry-run mode.

Design notes: The allocator exposes variables to control node affinity, max_pods, per-tenant min_reserved_gpus, and a fallback_policy that gracefully drains and migrates workloads before shrink. IAM roles were tightened: node pool roles are scoped to the tenant-specific service account with condition based on KMS key alias and VPC CIDR. Gateway has an explicit opt-in for cross-account peering (peering is disabled by default).

Migration plan: run tools/migrate-per-tenant-state --dry-run to validate; then run with --apply. The migrator creates a migration PR for state locks and records a migration manifest in state_migrations/<timestamp>-<tenant>.json. Rollback: migrator has --rollback that restores previous backend keys and re-attaches locks. The README contains a step-by-step checklist and estimated downtime (typically zero for control-plane, a few minutes for route propagation).

Testing and validation: added unit TF plan tests using terratest mock workspace, end-to-end smoke with a demo private deployment in the benchmark-lab account, and CI includes a validation job that runs the migrator in dry-run. One flaky test (gateway-route-propagation) was retried in CI once and passed.

Security and ops: default S3 lifecycle for state set to 7y; DynamoDB locks retained. Added output map with IAM principals for auditors. No secrets are stored in state.

Related: references ENG-1892 (tenant-segmentation initiative) and SUP-1087 (customer request). Also relates to PRs that introduced per-tenant billing tags but is independent.

Commits summary: 5 commits — add gateway module, add gpu allocator module, migrator utility and docs, tests and CI, followup fixes.

Files changed (high-level): modules/tenant_gateway/{main.tf,outputs.tf,variables.tf}, modules/gpu_allocator/{main.tf,alloc_policy.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf}, tools/migrate-per-tenant-state.py, examples/private/tenant-migration/README.md, tests/terratest/allocator_test.go, ci/pipelines/validate-migrator.yaml

Small code snippets included for reviewers: modules/gpu_allocator/alloc_policy.tf contains the allocator policy HCL (soft_reserve logic implemented in local variables + templatefile for k8s annotation), and modules/tenant_gateway/main.tf includes a tidied route table block with a condition to skip peering when var.enable_cross_account_peering = false.

Merge: squash+merge after approvals and passing CI.
